timing: Frozen after the autonomous eight paired runs completed, before opening their external development scores. The absence of live promotions motivates this follow-up.
question: Does a longer, cross-task memory provide better evidence than two future primary trials within one nine-fit run?
data: Only decisions, the feasible menus they saw and subsequently completed primary training-holdout results. Exclude the first exploration of each task: before any observations a common offset cannot compare exploration with an incumbent. No external labels or validation predictions.
method: Keep a version archive. The parent proposes bounded ridge corrections of its exploration score forecasts from the residuals of previously observed tasks. Features are intercept, novelty and inverse square root of the number of prior primary observations. Each new version must pass delayed evaluation on entire, distinct tasks. Accepted versions can propose a successor, and increase the next correction step by 25 percent; rejected proposals halve the next step. The observed task is added to memory only after the decision.

fit_from: both previously observed released training histories

gate: Per task compute mean absolute forecasting error on future measured explorations after cold start. Accept a generation if unweighted mean task gain is at least 0.003, no task loss exceeds 0.02, and at least one feasible menu's leading action changes. Freeze versions before challenge. Record candidate and parent predictions and all rejections. Historic feedback only supports measured actions; hypothetical rank changes do not establish classifier gains.
release_rule: This retrospective study cannot replace the pinned submission baseline.
